```yaml
requirements:
  - id: S-1
    text: "The top-level module is c12_nexys_pwm_audio_top and exposes the board-XDC ports for AUD_PWM, AUD_SD, USB-UART, CLK100MHZ, CPU_RESETN, and the 16-bit LED output, plus the CLKS_PER_BIT, TIMEOUT_CYCLES, and BUILD_STAMP parameters."
    proof: [analysis, simulation]
    modules: []
  - id: S-2
    text: "The sample is a signed 16-bit value that can be written over the shell, is held between writes, and is cleared by CPU_RESETN; sample_out is a combinational signed 16-bit result."
    proof: [simulation]
    modules: []
  - id: S-3
    text: "The gain register is unsigned Q15, resets to 2068, accepts shell writes, and stores 8192 instead of any written value greater than 8192."
    proof: [simulation]
    modules: []
  - id: S-4
    text: "sample_out equals floor(sample multiplied by gain divided by 32768), with the result represented as a signed 16-bit value."
    proof: [simulation, analysis]
    modules: []
  - id: S-5
    text: "A free-running 10-bit counter advances from the 100 MHz clock and repeats every 1024 clocks, giving a nominal 97.7 kHz PWM carrier."
    proof: [simulation, analysis]
    modules: []
  - id: S-6
    text: "The PWM duty value is 512 plus floor(sample_out divided by 128), and is updated once per PWM period."
    proof: [simulation, analysis]
    modules: []
  - id: S-7
    text: "AUD_PWM is pulled low when the PWM counter is greater than or equal to the duty value and is otherwise high impedance; it is never driven high."
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
    modules: []
  - id: S-8
    text: "AUD_SD is always high."
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
    modules: []
  - id: S-9
    text: "The 16-bit LED output is always off."
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
    modules: []
  - id: S-10
    text: "The shell communicates over the USB-UART at 115200 baud and supports writing the sample, writing the gain, and reading back sample_out."
    proof: [simulation, hardware]
    modules: []
  - id: S-11
    text: "The design closes timing at 100 MHz."
    proof: [analysis, hardware]
    modules: []
  - id: S-12
    text: "Simulation verifies reset behavior, gain writes of 65535, 4000, 8192, and 8193, a reset after a write, and sample values including 0, +32767, and -32768 held for several PWM periods; it checks sample_out, low-clock counts measured at AUD_PWM, and AUD_SD."
    proof: [simulation]
    modules: []
  - id: S-13
    text: "The top-level exposes CLKS_PER_BIT, TIMEOUT_CYCLES, and BUILD_STAMP as parameters, and introduces no other time constants."
    proof: [analysis]
    modules: []
questions:
  - question: "What shell command framing, command encodings, numeric formats, and response format should be used for sample writes, gain writes, and sample_out reads?"
    default: "Use line-oriented ASCII commands: S followed by a signed decimal sample, G followed by an unsigned decimal gain, and R to read sample_out; return one line per command with a result or error."
    reason: "The specification requires these shell operations and the baud rate but does not define the protocol the shell and design must share."
    settles: [S-1, S-2, S-3, S-10]
  - question: "When should a changed duty value take effect, and what PWM counter and duty state should be used at reset?"
    default: "Reset the counter to zero and duty to 512; capture the calculated duty at counter rollover so it applies for the following period."
    reason: "The specification says duty is updated once per period but does not define the update boundary or initial PWM phase."
    settles: [S-5, S-6]
  - question: "Should CPU_RESETN assertion and release be synchronous or asynchronous to CLK100MHZ?"
    default: "Use asynchronous assertion and synchronize deassertion to CLK100MHZ."
    reason: "The specification requires reset behavior but does not define reset synchronization."
    settles: [S-2, S-3, S-5]
```
